h66d13fee0c1a:
Gather assets scattered across everywhere
into one library you can always find your way back to
ha2ee4b267ede: Design files, RAW photos, videos, 3D models, fonts, PDFs—drop them into TuKu and you can view, search, edit, and drag them straight out. Everything happens on your machine: no uploads, and it works just as well offline.
hc9d4fd710ce0: See what it can actually do → First, see where it falls short
hcb30b693c7e1:
In a head-to-head review of 8 similar products, it ranks 1st for local-only use (90.9 out of 100; Eagle in second place at 82.1).
        The basis is an audit of 137,000 lines of code plus reproducible benchmark data.
h077566a15b4a: It solves these very concrete, everyday annoyances
h2186bf3a10b2: No talk of "empowerment" or "ecosystems"—just the little stalls you hit every day.
h359dda193ab2: You dug through six folders to find one reference image
hfcfb3e0a842f: Assets are scattered across Downloads, the desktop, WeChat, cloud drives, and external disks, so in the end you rummage around thinking "I'm sure I saved it last week."
h67358d5ec586: The same image exists in three copies; you edit one and forget the other two
h7d35dc047f27: Without a library there's no single copy of record, and after an edit you can't tell which file is current.
ha41a7c52eb1d: PSDs, RAWs, and 3D files all show up as blank icons
h4e88120551c9: You can only guess the contents from the file name; opening one takes a dozen seconds, and after ten you've lost patience.
h63008ce43e7f: A hundred images need resizing and watermarking—one at a time
h62e05e90a120: Batch work risks overwriting the originals, and if you get it wrong there's no way to roll back.
h324b70d555fc: You remember "blue hour, seaside, backlit"—but not the file name
h17a97b081f81: The file is IMG_4821 and the folder is "New folder (2)"; keyword search finds nothing.
h858638da13e1: A client wants to see the proposal, so you send a ZIP
ha3dc82d041fa: They unzip a pile of loose images with no order, no notes, and no clue what you're presenting.
h31a44ad78402: Eight areas of features, ordered the way you actually work

h71d87d3dab59: Watched folders: point it at a few folders and anything dropped in is added automatically.

h187cccf478a6: 23 watermarks and 20 frames, plus a phone-model library of nearly a thousand entries refreshed quarterly.

hde0810d94a8b: Windows live wallpaper: set images from your library as the desktop directly.

h7556714586ac: File associations are set up automatically, and asset folders changed outside the app refresh automatically.
h3eebb6fc8dc3: Automate callable by scripts and AI

hc2cd30e85d90: Good for bulk organizing, automatic archiving, and plugging into your company's internal workflows.

hbf1f6f5c8f10: Eight things other products don't have, or don't do well
h420859f292c2: These are what really set it apart from an ordinary image viewer—and why it's worth installing on its own.
h6ee42b3d3e0e: Chinese substring search: type two characters and it's there
h21a2a435f783: Keyword search in most libraries requires complete words or word segmentation; type "seaside su" and "seaside sunset backlit" won't be found. This uses a character-level index that matches at any position, which matters most for Chinese.
ha1a9ee63a16f: Why it's rare: staying fast without word segmentation for Chinese takes a lot of extra work on the index, and most products simply give up on it.
h5fe25875dd68: Find it by what you remember seeing: on-device semantic search
hca3cb0dfcbea: You've forgotten the file name, the tags, even the year, but you remember "that blue-toned one, someone standing by a window." Search with a single description and get results in 47 ms across a 20,000-image library.
h74707815b397: Why it's rare: the model runs on your own machine—no image uploads, and no cloud quota burned.
hb4d298bde535: Drag it out ready to use: a direct line to design software
h89057a3ad84c: Select an asset and drag it onto a Photoshop canvas or into Figma; it lands as an image. No "export to the desktop, then drag it again."
h9c6a9bdfd5a5: Why it's rare: browser-based products structurally can't do this, and desktop products that could usually don't bother.
hb52e73ca645c: Turn your library into a Windows live wallpaper
h005eb062f5a3: Rotate images from a chosen folder on your desktop, with configurable interval and order. Designers and content creators clearly feel their assets come alive.
hb74359fd27e7: Why it's rare: it means drawing into the system's desktop layer—a classic "works, but is a pain" feature.
h4f1414d22c0c: Show colleagues your images without the cloud
h452109c3d9d7: Read-only LAN sharing: generate a link and anyone on the same network can browse your selection in a browser, with a password, an optional expiry, and downloads that can be blocked.
hf1c186f88a20: Why it's rare: most products turn sharing into a doorway to their cloud service, and local-first products often skip it entirely.
h3d5b3babcec5: Edit images without destroying originals: operation log + dual-stack undo
hb53ad27779c5: Crops, color adjustments, and watermarks are all "recorded entries"; the original file stays byte-for-byte intact. If you don't like the result, undo all the way back—and redo again.
h57e7e97e7ede: Why it's rare: true non-destructive editing means changing the whole storage model, and many products just "auto-back up a copy, then overwrite."
hbe85e781bcc2: Let your AI assistant read your asset library directly
h6aa82441f746: 11 built-in MCP tools let AI clients search, tag, and archive on your instructions—not just chat about it, but actually do it.
h060a5fce2e66: Why it's rare: it amounts to opening up your own data interface, which most commercial products aren't willing to do.
hc9d5066e7031: A 20,000-image library that still scrolls smoothly
haa5b20768ccb: Scrolling isn't "load everything at once": pages use keyset cursors, the index uses SQLite full-text, and thumbnails are cached. 7 ms for the list, 11 ms for deep pages.
h0ac36418bbfb: Why it's rare: most similar products start spinning at the 20,000-image mark.
ha50682fde77b: Is it fast? These numbers say enough
h986b23857e4f: All measured (Windows, a 20,000-asset library), not theoretical. Lower is better.
h0689bc6b354f: Building a library is "pour it in and wait a bit," not waiting all night
h00645b58641e: There on click—no spinner in sight
hefdfbedccf95: Describe the scene in one sentence; results within a blink
h80dbcc8bace5: Color editing on large images still works, no freeze
h856942897aef: For reference, a human blink is roughly 100–400 ms. The figures above are medians from the audited environment; million-scale libraries are not yet validated—see "Limitations" in the next section.
hd14310897f02: Up and running in three steps
hd90f9e7d6258: No manual to read first, and no need to organize your assets before starting—its design premise is "collect it messy first, sort it later."
hcd0546d4a5f9: Download the Windows installer from the release page and double-click to install. If Windows shows "Unknown publisher" on first run, click "More info → Run anyway."
hbd43fd76363b: Pick an empty folder as your asset library. A local disk with plenty of space is recommended; avoid cloud-sync folders—sync software makes the library rescan over and over.
h86f40fb60c5f: Drag files or whole folders into the window, or let it watch your Downloads folder. Once thumbnails finish, you can search, filter, and drag assets out.
h30837f1dfb25: Space for a quick preview without double-clicking; Ctrl+F to search, Ctrl+Z to undo (up to 200 steps).
h2654f88cf271: Let thumbnails finish before starting AI analysis; the two queues run separately so they don't fight over the CPU.
hd7755c3112ed: 173 built-in onboarding tutorials; the first launch guides you automatically, and you can turn them off anytime.
h02a245c8a762: The library lock only guards "opening this library"; it doesn't encrypt files on disk—treat it as a door badge, not a safe.
he3b3e893720e: Who it suits, and who it doesn't
h20aa2944f0e7: One paragraph to decide is more useful than ten screenshots.
h4ab503f68f81: You do design / photography / content work solo on one Windows PC.
h788d23a04d8c: You have tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of assets, mostly on local or external disks.
hc29d99356405: You need bulk organizing, batch processing, and packaged delivery.
hda07d4ed67ab: You want scripts or AI clients to work directly with your asset library.
hebe56875f7d2: You care about assets not being uploaded and formats not being held hostage.
h300c9b342447: Typical users: freelance designers, editors running their own channels, and photography enthusiasts who manage a reference library.
h2d8c9cf11f28: It genuinely doesn't fit yet if
hc406e8ddfc53: A team shares one asset collection and needs permissions and approvals.
h8b0f0b1e70d6: Your main machine is a mac or Linux.
h122f2a610cac: You need to browse the library from a phone anywhere, or want automatic cloud sync.
hbdda006aaef9: You need an English interface for overseas colleagues.
h6dbc803b3ff5: You need to manage a million-scale library out of the box.
h5e2dcaa56a08: These five aren't "we'll make do for now" cases—they genuinely aren't possible at this stage, and all are listed under "Limitations" in the next section.
h764c47eca76e: Let's be clear first about where it still falls short
hb7b4cff62f23: An introduction that only lists strengths isn't much use. Here are its real current weak spots, and why they exist.
hacc4dd98a6e3: Windows only. There are build scripts for mac / Linux, but no real-device validation, so support isn't claimed.
h9c3b877c6dbe: No cloud sync, no mobile app. The closest substitute is read-only LAN sharing—view images on the same network, but not beyond it.
hddd45dc8bf0c: No multi-person collaboration. No accounts, member permissions, or approval flows; the workaround is an export package plus read-only links.
he43897bd10ce: Chinese interface only. There's no translation layer; interface strings live directly in the components.
h95d3df8a042d: Validated at 20,000 images; million-scale is untested. The timeline, list, people view, and main library grid all render windowed, and layout calculation now appends incrementally—scrolling no longer slows as the library grows; but a million assets is a target, not a promise.
hb4a8d605492d: The first import with AI enabled is slow. The model runs on your local CPU, and the model files must be downloaded the first time; semantic and face indexing that can't finish during the day can be handled by "overnight batch processing" during idle hours, but the first night still means waiting.
h1afa168a26fc: The installer is large and has no code signing. v1.2.16 trimmed about 200MB of unused cross-platform inference libraries, but it's still large overall; the first run gets flagged by Windows SmartScreen and needs manual approval.
hdbf7a3c0548e: Why do these gaps exist? This is a one-person project: there's no server budget and no second person's time. Cloud sync and multi-person collaboration aren't "impossible to write"—but once built, you'd be on the hook every month for storage, bandwidth, backups, and outages— that's an ongoing expense, not a feature in a release. So they're scheduled as long-term goals, not marketing lines.
hd164c9185d3c: The order for these four (do the free ones first, then let revenue decide how far cloud goes):
hb9e500f709f5: Step one: extract the copy into string entries and freeze them—no cost, no cloud dependency
hae00f3c48a2f: Step two: real-device smoke test → installer → platform difference list; Linux deferred
ha56bb0980cbd: Step three: read-only multi-device → accounts and incremental sync → conflict merging
h0590cbd28a42: Step four: comments → member permissions → approval flows (plugin marketplace not promised)
h9020a5aa4705: Count these four in as well, and the 17-item score is 71.2, ranking 3rd among the 8 products (1st for local-only use). With all four at target, it's 87.1. All these numbers and the algorithms are written up in the full review report, verifiable item by item.
hc4ac5de24601: It may be exactly right for you—or completely wrong
h2b1eb7a66ca6:
If you nod at more than three lines in the "it fits" column, it's worth installing and trying—your assets stay on your own disk,
    and uninstalling the software won't remove or damage your files.
    If any line in the "doesn't fit" column applies to you, don't force it: the review also lists what each of the other 7 products is suited for.
